extracted.intended_audience: mid-career researchers preparing an application for the Wellcome Career Development Award (Discovery Research)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility/assessment criteria for applicants seeking a Wellcome Career Development Award to lead a substantial, innovative research programme (Discovery Research). Covers who can apply, how proposals are assessed, what costs are allowable, and host organisation responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead applicant career stage and aims
rubrics_metrics.description: This scheme provides funding for mid-career researchers from any discipline who have the potential to be international research leaders. You must be ready to lead a substantial and innovative research programme and aim to make a key contribution to your field by generating significant shifts in understanding and/or developing methodologies, conceptual frameworks, tools or techniques that could benefit health-related research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the award we expect you to develop research capabilities and leadership skills, support others to undertake research responsibly and promote a positive and inclusive culture, and start training the next generation of researchers. By the end of the award you should have achieved international standing and be able to apply for permanent positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-initial-training research experience
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible you will already be driving your own research and must have completed one or two substantial periods of research after your initial research training and made important contributions to your area of research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You will probably have experience of working collaboratively and may have directed, or closely guided, the work of others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractual appointment & salary eligibility rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Salary eligibility depends on your contractual circumstances at point of application: applicants appointed to their first permanent/open-ended/long-term rolling contract within the last three years may not request salary (unless in LMIC and need external funding). Applicants on fixed-term positions with four years or less remaining may request salary. Fixed-term positions with more than four years left cannot request salary and host must underwrite salary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions and allowances exist if time away from research, part-time roles, changes of discipline, or LMIC appointment norms apply. If contract changes between application and award activation you must tell Wellcome. If after two or more years of award activation your organisation gives you a permanent contract that includes salary, you may keep the salary element to use towards remaining research costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum research time contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: You must be able to contribute at least 80% of your research time to the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requesting your salary on the award you should not spend more than 20% of your time on non-research activities (teaching, administration, clinical duties). If in a clinical craft speciality you may spend up to 40% on clinical duties. If not requesting salary you should spend sufficient time on research to support your team and achieve proposed aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor requirements and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Your sponsor must be an individual at your administering organisation holding an established post (or honorary academic appointment) for the duration of the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsor must guarantee the space and resources you'll need, ensure the research environment supports completion, confirm workload expectations (including limits on non-research time if salary requested), organise a discussion about your future at the organisation, and, if you plan to work >3 months outside host organisation, arrange an additional sponsor at that location. Sponsors are not paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You should identify a mentor for the award period who has a track record in training and mentorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentor should support and guide you on managing your application, developing your research career and personal development, and managing processes and regulations at your host organisation. Sponsor can also be mentor. Mentors are not paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborator roles and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborators support delivery of the project but don't lead a specific component; they do not have to meet eligibility requirements and are not required to give a minimum research time commitment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborators cannot receive a salary or compensation for time on the project. You can request costs to cover collaborators' expenses (travel, materials) directly related to the research and justified in application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current Wellcome grantholders eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Current grantholders of certain mid-career Wellcome schemes (e.g., Sir Henry Dale Fellowships, Research Career Development Fellowships, Intermediate Clinical Fellowships, etc.) may apply to this scheme until the end of their awards unless they have been appointed to an equivalent permanent contract they will take up by the start of the Career Development Award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one of these grantholders you must have an active grant at the application deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent Wellcome awards policy
rubrics_metrics.description: During a Career Development Award you cannot be the sole applicant on any other Wellcome awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can be a coapplicant on other Wellcome awards provided you can justify how you will manage commitments across awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If unsuccessful with an application to this scheme you can submit one more application for the same project; significant changes are needed for the second application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You do not need to contact Wellcome before resubmitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: You are not eligible if you hold, have held, or have accepted an offer for an equivalent award at this career stage (exceptions for current Wellcome grantholders) or if you have made an application to this scheme and are waiting for a decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You cannot apply to carry out activities that involve the transfer of grant funds into mainland China.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research scope and fit with Discovery Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Your research must fit within what Wellcome supports in Discovery Research and have the potential to improve human life, health and wellbeing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research can be in any discipline (STEM, experimental medicine, humanities/social sciences, clinical/allied health, public health). It must not fall outside Discovery Research scope and must not start earlier than seven months after the application deadline. Applicants should check 'what we fund' and 'what we don't fund'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administering organisation location and type
rubrics_metrics.description: The administering organisation must be based in the UK, Republic of Ireland, or a low- or middle-income country (apart from India and mainland China) and must be not-for-profit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible organisation types include higher education institutions, research institutes, and healthcare organisations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administering organisation obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Administering organisation must guarantee they will either provide you with a permanent/open-ended/long-term rolling contract by the end of the award OR carry out a formal review process no less than two years before the end of your award to discuss your future, including possibility of such a contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This does not apply to applicants who already have a permanent/open-ended contract. If administering organisation is core-funded, the Career Development Award should not replace or reduce existing/planned core support. Grants must be administered at an organisation that can sign up to Wellcome grant conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding amount guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: You should ask for the resources you need for your research programme and work with your organisation to justify the request. Annual expenditure for a Career Development Award is usually below £250,000 excluding the applicant's salary; applications above this value will be subject to additional scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost the application at 1.0 FTE; Wellcome will extend duration for part-time awards accordingly. You can only hold one of these awards; no renewals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding duration and part-time rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The award usually lasts for 8 years but may be less for some disciplines and may only be longer if held part-time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applying, cost at 1.0 (100%) FTE and Wellcome will extend duration to reflect part-time working.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coapplicants not accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Coapplicants are not accepted on this scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be sole lead applicants; collaborators can be named but not coapplicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary provision and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Wellcome will provide your salary if you do not have a post or you have a temporary or fixed-term post with four years or less remaining on your contract. If you have a permanent post, you can only ask for your salary if you are based in a low- or middle-income country and have to get your salary from external grant funding, and your administering organisation confirms this and underwrites the salary/post for the grant duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wellcome will fund the total cost of your salary for the entire period of the grant and you can only receive one salary. Host must confirm you need external funding for salary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary cost components and inflation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Salary should be based on host pay scales and include basic salary, employer's contributions (statutory obligations and pension), incremental progression and locally recognised allowances (e.g., London allowance). Do not include promotion costs or prior Wellcome fellowship supplements. Allow for salary pay awards during Year 1 using agreed pay awards or IMF 'inflation, average consumer price' if unknown; from Year 2 onwards Wellcome provides an automatic salary inflation allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If host is LMIC and you'll be working in a high-income country for ≥12 months, you should be paid at an appropriate rate for that country according to age/experience. Clinical academics' salaries should be appropriate to clinical status and within relevant academic/senior clinical lecturer scales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching buyout for humanities and social sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: HSS researchers can ask for funds for teaching replacement to cover the cost of a temporary replacement lecturer but must retain at least a 10% commitment to teaching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs can cover up to 33% FTE of contracted time, usually for a more junior person, and can be spread across the grant. If you already get buyout costs from another grant you can ask for this cost but only for the period when you won't receive buyout from the other grant. You must provide a letter from your employer confirming a teaching commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visa and work permit costs for grantholder
rubrics_metrics.description: If Wellcome pays your salary on the grant you can ask for visa and work permit costs to help you take up the post; this may include costs for partner and dependent children, Immigration Health Surcharge where appropriate, and essential associated costs (travel to visa appointments, English tests) if justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award holders who need a visa to work in the UK may be eligible for the Global Talent Visa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff funding limits and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Wellcome will cover salary costs for up to 4 Full-Time Equivalent (FTE) staff (full or part-time) employed on your project. You can ask for more staff costs if you need specialist service staff or technical experts, or support for disability-related adjustments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PhD/Research Masters fees can be requested only for research staff employed on the grant (up to two research staff). Research staff should be hired to undertake specific research activities; if fees not requested at application stage they cannot be repurposed later.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to cost salaries for research staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff salaries should be appropriate to skills and responsibilities and calculated using host organisation salary scales. Costs should include basic salary, employer contributions (statutory obligations and pension), Apprentice Levy charges for UK salaries, incremental progression and locally recognised allowances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow for pay awards during Year 1 (use IMF 'inflation, average consumer price' if unknown). From Year 2 use organisation's current pay rates; Wellcome provides a separate inflation allowance for salary inflation costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disability-related adjustment support
rubrics_metrics.description: You can ask for adjustment support if you or a staff member is disabled or has a long-term health condition. Costs can include additional staff to help with day-to-day activities, assistive technology, and care costs for assistance animals when travel is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wellcome will not pay for capital/building costs (e.g., access ramps). You can only ask for these costs if your government/employer does not cover them or only covers some; Wellcome will meet only the shortfall. If you don't know costs now you can ask for them after award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing professional development and training costs
rubrics_metrics.description: You can ask for contributions towards continuing professional development and professional skills training (research leadership, people management, career development, responsible conduct, diversity/inclusion, healthy research culture, environmental impact).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your administering organisation is expected to provide and fund this training; if not available or quality inadequate, you can ask for up to £500/year for you and each staff member who meets criteria (post ≥12 months and ≥50% FTE on Wellcome awards). Costs must be justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research skills training costs
rubrics_metrics.description: You can ask for costs to cover technical and research skills training needed to deliver your proposed research for you and each member of staff employed on your grant who will be in a post of ≥12 months and working ≥50% FTE on Wellcome-funded awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must justify these costs in your application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials and consumables coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Wellcome will pay for materials and consumables needed to carry out your project, including laboratory chemicals and materials, project-specific PPE above expected standard, printing associated with fieldwork and empirical research, and associated shipping/delivery/freight charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should justify consumables in the context of the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animals costs and conditions (full economic costing organisations)
rubrics_metrics.description: If your organisation uses full economic costing you can ask for funds to buy animals if essential, and Wellcome will fund charge-out rates for animal house facilities covering running costs (maintenance, experimental procedures, licences, training), appropriate estates costs, cage and equipment depreciation (not building depreciation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If research in UK uses macaques they must be sourced from MRC Centre for Macaques. Wellcome may not pay full charge-out if it has significantly funded the facility's infrastructure/core support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animals costs and conditions (non-full economic costing organisations)
rubrics_metrics.description: If your organisation does not use full economic costing you can ask for costs covering buying/transporting animals, running costs (maintenance, procedures, licences, training), staff costs (e.g., animal house technicians), equipment maintenance, housing equipment specific to project, microbiological monitoring, waste disposal, licences, training and enrichment costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In these cases Wellcome will not provide estates costs, cage/building depreciation costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment purchase eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: You can ask for equipment purchase where it is not available at your administering organisation or through collaborations and you will be the main user with at least 50% of use for Wellcome-funded activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes small multi-use items. Costs may include purchase, delivery, installation, maintenance and training. Second-hand equipment is allowed if more environmentally sustainable. Wellcome will cover VAT/import duties where usual UK exemptions don't apply or for non-UK applicants who can't recover such costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment maintenance eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Wellcome will cover maintenance costs for equipment that is funded by Wellcome or another source, essential to the proposed project, five years old (or will become five years old during the grant), and cost-effective and environmentally sustainable to maintain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintenance can be requested for small multi-user equipment if at least 50% use is for Wellcome-funded activities and there is no mechanism to recoup costs through access charges. Wellcome will not provide maintenance support where a mechanism exists to recoup costs through access charges for all other equipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer equipment and software
rubrics_metrics.description: Wellcome will cover cost of one personal computer or laptop per person working on the grant (reasonable, market-rate, justified), software, software licences and other recurring computing costs linked to the project, and Electronic Research Notebook/ELN software per user per year for the duration of a Wellcome project (approved by your organisation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wellcome will not pay for significantly expensive items unless justified, installation or training costs, or access charges for computing resources. Cannot claim ERN/ELN hardware or organisation-wide ERN/ELN software beyond per user/year basis on your project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access charges for shared equipment/facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: You can ask for the cost of access to shared equipment, facilities or services if essential to your project, which may include materials/consumables plus a proportion of maintenance and service contracts and staff time for dedicated technical staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wellcome does not cover estates and utilities, depreciation or insurance, or contributions towards departmental technical/administrative/management staff time (except animal housing facilities where applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overheads eligibility and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: You can ask for overheads if your administering organisation is a higher education institution, healthcare organisation or research institute outside the UK, or a UK research organisation that does not receive core funding for overheads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overheads can include estates and non-project dedicated administrative/support staff; total overheads requested should not be more than 20% of costs requested and must directly support the activity. Sub-award overheads are allowed except UK universities can't ask for overheads on sub-contracted activity if their university includes it in Charity Research Support Fund reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to apply for overheads (Finance Director letter)
rubrics_metrics.description: In your grant application you must include a letter from your Finance Director stating how overhead costs were calculated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If organisation has externally audited/verified methodology include confirmation of validated rate, how the rate was arrived at, when last reviewed, and where details can be found. If not, include a breakdown of costs and confirmation request truly represents incurred costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmentally conscious travel policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Travel on grants should be done in an environmentally conscious way in line with Wellcome's environmental sustainability policy; consider video conferencing or virtual attendance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can ask for low carbon transport even if more expensive (e.g., train instead of flying). Economy flights allowed when train >10 hours or not possible due to availability, safety, visa issues, disability, long-term health or caring requirements; Wellcome will not pay business class. You can ask for project-related alternatives to travel and costs to mitigate carbon emissions (accredited carbon credits) with organisational approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference attendance limits and caring costs
rubrics_metrics.description: You can ask for contribution to attending meetings and conferences: Grantholder – £2,000 a year; Research/technical staff – £1,000 each a year. Caring costs for conference attendance can be provided (up to £1,000 per person per conference) if Wellcome provides the salary and conference is directly related to research and costs are over and above normal care and not covered by organisers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can also ask for accredited carbon credits to mitigate conference travel emissions in addition to these limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other essential travel and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: You can ask for travel and subsistence costs for collaborative visits, essential visits (facilities, host organisations, sample collection, fieldwork). Each visit and its duration must be justified in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partners and dependants travel rules apply (see partner/dependants entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Partners and dependants travel allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: If travelling overseas and away for more than 12 months, Wellcome will provide travel costs for your partner and any dependants if they travel with you; may provide for shorter trips if justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partner defined as married or cohabiting ≥1 year and sharing some joint financial commitment (e.g., mortgage).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outward/return travel mode preference
rubrics_metrics.description: Where travel is necessary, people are expected to travel by train for end-to-end journeys of 10 hours or less; flights paid when train not available, safety/visa issues, disability/caring needs, or journey >10 hours. Wellcome will not pay for business class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can ask for carbon mitigation costs for journeys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accommodation and subsistence rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to one month away: subsistence (accommodation, meals, incidentals) using employer rates or HMRC rates. 1–12 months: reasonable rental costs only (aparthotels allowed) with expectation to choose economical options. If from LMIC and working in high-income country 1–12 months, can ask up to £10/day extra. >12 months: Wellcome will pay housing costs (see overseas allowances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss appropriate rates with administering and employing organisations or Wellcome as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baggage and freight shipping allowances
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to 12 months away: up to 80kg additional baggage/unaccompanied freight for outward and return journeys. More than 12 months: costs of shipping personal items at beginning and end of overseas work (half container if travelling alone; whole 20ft container if travelling with partner/dependants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits and justifications required per duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical, travel insurance and emergency evacuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Wellcome will pay medical and travel insurance for travel outside home country where state healthcare not accessible for the trip. They do not pay medical insurance for trips to UK/RoI. For UK trips ≤6 months take travel insurance; for >6 months Wellcome covers Immigration Health Surcharge. If working in low-/middle-income country Wellcome will cover emergency evacuation costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wellcome will cover insurance/tax aspects where visa costs may be taxable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visas, vaccinations and mandatory healthcare costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Wellcome will pay costs of visas, vaccinations and anti-malaria treatment, including costs to access the healthcare system required for immigration (e.g., Immigration Health Surcharge in the UK).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If already in country visa costs may be taxable; Wellcome will cover any tax related to these costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Housing security costs in LMIC locations
rubrics_metrics.description: If based in a low- or middle-income country for >1 month and necessary, you can ask for housing security costs (guards, panic buttons, alarms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask your employing organisation for advice on level of security needed and justify costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overseas allowances for ≥12 month stays
rubrics_metrics.description: If you or staff will spend >12 months in another country, Wellcome will help with additional costs of working overseas (over and above standard travel/subsistence) as a contribution towards personal cost and assuming you will pay income tax in home or host country and that allowances are not provided from elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowances can include partners/dependants travel, accommodation/housing, and education costs where local provision is not equivalent. Applicants must provide estimated costs as accurately as possible; Wellcome may set maxima per location based on market data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education costs for dependants when overseas
rubrics_metrics.description: You can ask for local nursery or school fees where there isn't free local education of the same standard as in your home country; costs include local nursery up to 30 hours/week for 3–4 year olds, and local junior/secondary school fees (text truncated on page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Education allowances are considered part of overseas allowances and must be justified and in line with Wellcome policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment weightings and proposal quality descriptors
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are reviewed on research proposal (50%), your skills and experience (25%), and your research environment (25%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research proposal: expected to be Bold (aims to deliver significant shift or advance), Creative (novel approach, new concepts/methods or novel combination), and High quality (well-designed, clear, evidenced, feasible outcomes). Skills and experience: review outputs, contributions to developing other researchers, leadership/management skills and plans to develop them during award. Research environment: review how you will contribute to strategic aims, how environment will help develop capabilities and leadership, and contribution to positive/inclusive research culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start date / project start restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Your research must not start earlier than seven months after the application deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure project timelines in application reflect this constraint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual conference and travel caring support eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Wellcome will provide costs to cover caring responsibilities if you or staff employed on your grant attend a conference, under conditions: Wellcome provides the salary, conference is directly related to research, caring costs are over and above normal care, and conference organiser/employer unable to cover costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can ask for up to £1,000 per person for each conference.
